title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
source: canonical Longest Repeating Character Replacement concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is a string s of uppercase letters and an integer k. You may change at most k characters of s to any letter. Return the length of the longest single-letter run that can exist after those changes.

examples.explanation: Changing both B characters (or both A characters) turns the whole string into one letter.
With no changes allowed the existing run of four A characters is the answer.

hints: A window can become one repeated letter when window length minus the count of its most common character is at most k.
When a window stops being fixable, shrinking from the left restores feasibility; the window never needs to grow past its best size.
Sweep right, counting letters in the window. While (window length - max count) > k, advance left. Track the largest valid window length.
solution: Sliding window over s with a frequency count. A window is fixable when its length minus its most common character count is at most k; otherwise slide the left edge forward. Because the window only ever grows or slides, one pass suffices: O(n) time with O(26) counts, so O(n) time and O(1) space.
failureHint: hidden tests include k = 0, all-distinct letters, and long runs already in place
